_comment: Chip-Backed Finance Observatory - monitoring configuration. Edit keywords, feeds and publication mode here; never edit watch.py. After changing terms, run: python3 -m unittest discover tests
_auto_publish_mode_options: off = candidates only; the workflow opens a GitHub issue and the curator adds real deals by hand (recommended) | direct = also append entries to observatory-data.json as PENDING REVIEW (listed apart on the site, never counted). Any other value is treated as off.
_terms_comment: Matching is whole-word and case-insensitive; a plural s/es is allowed automatically; a trailing * makes a prefix. strong_phrases match in title or summary. The other rules look at the TITLE only: tech_terms + finance_terms, or context_terms + strong_finance_terms. exclude_terms in the title always reject. A watched issuer name (config 'issuers') counts like a tech term. Every match must also carry a deal signal: an amount ($2.4B, 100 million) or one of deal_verbs, in the title (for a strong phrase, title or summary). This drops commentary and explainers about GPU financing. Exception: a title with a stress_term plus a chip/issuer term plus a finance term is kept without a deal signal.
_issuers_comment: Companies whose financings we track. A watched name in a headline counts like a chip term (issuers write 'CoreWeave closes $2.6bn loan', not 'GPU'). Names also drive story grouping. With a cik, the watcher reads the company's EDGAR filing list (8-K items in edgar_8k_items, periodic reports, and IPO registration statements, whose debt sections list every facility). match_case: true matches the name case-sensitively (IREN, not the Italian utility Iren). Check a new cik at https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=<cik>; the watcher skips a cik whose EDGAR name does not match.
_edgar_8k_items_comment: 1.01 material agreement, 1.02 its termination, 2.03 new financial obligation, 2.04 acceleration (default), 2.06 impairment.
_market_terms_comment: Stock-market chatter about a watched company ("CoreWeave leads tech stocks in rally after earnings eased debt fears") passes the loose combo rule. market_terms reject combo matches only, never strong phrases or stress signals.
_known_lenders_comment: Used by the curator page to prefill the Lenders field (autofill.py). Add names as you meet them.
_stress_comment: Stress signals (defaults, seizures, downgrades) are what the observatory exists to catch, so they skip the deal-signal rule. A headline with a stress term plus a chip/issuer term plus a finance term is kept and listed in its own digest section.
_edgar_comment: One candidate per filing. Forms below are skipped (fund prospectuses, proxy and merger filings, ownership reports). edgar_max_hits caps paging per query; the digest says TRUNCATED when it is reached.
_edgar_fulltext_forms_comment: Full-text hits on other forms (prospectuses, registration statements, structured notes) are mostly risk-factor boilerplate. They are kept only when they match at least edgar_min_queries_other_forms different queries (e.g. a neocloud IPO prospectus).
_press_release_comment: GlobeNewswire's RSS refuses automated clients (HTTP 403), so press-release wires are searched through Google News instead. CoreWeave and Blue Owl IR feeds sit behind a bot challenge (we do not work around it). PR Newswire's financing feed only holds about a day of items, too shallow for a weekly run. The Nvidia newsroom holds about a week.
tier1_google_news_queries: GPU financing site:prnewswire.com OR site:businesswire.com OR site:globenewswire.com
GPU-backed OR "secured by GPUs" site:prnewswire.com OR site:businesswire.com OR site:globenewswire.com
GPU OR "AI infrastructure" OR "data center" rating site:moodys.com OR site:spglobal.com OR site:fitchratings.com OR site:kbra.com OR site:dbrsmorningstar.com
tier2_google_news_queries: CoreWeave OR Lambda OR Crusoe OR Fluidstack OR Nscale debt OR loan OR facility
GPU lender default OR seized OR restructuring
"delayed draw term loan" GPU OR "AI infrastructure"
_google_news_editions_comment: Editions for the tier-2 queries (the default is en-US). In a 60-day test run (2026-11-13) en-IN added a few new items; en-GB and en-SG added almost none, so they are left out. Non-English editions would need translated terms in the relevance filter, which it does not have yet.
